name: Mexico
note: Traveler-focused Mexico pack (civil-law country). Emergencies, police & bribery, if detained, drugs, driving/insurance, entry/FMM, consular rights. Verify before relying; not local legal advice.

getLawyer.why: If arrested or detained in Mexico, you have the right to a lawyer and to contact your embassy — do both immediately. Pre-trial detention is common and can be long. Say nothing and sign nothing without a lawyer and interpreter.

If an officer demands cash: you can refuse to hand over money or your passport, note the officer's name/badge/patrol number, say you will call 911, and ask for a written fine or to go to the nearest police station. Do not pay roadside.
Drug penalties are severe (long prison sentences), and cannabis rules are unclear — you can be arrested or extorted. Contact your embassy and a local lawyer immediately; say nothing without counsel.

deadlines.title: Tourist stay — up to 180 days (officer sets it)
deadlines.rule: Visa-free tourist stays up to 180 DAYS, but the officer sets your actual permitted days (may be fewer). Complete the FMMD online on arrival and KEEP it. Extensions are not possible from inside Mexico; overstaying brings fines, detention, or deportation.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Mexico

deadlines.title: Mexican liability insurance is mandatory
deadlines.rule: Canadian auto insurance is NOT valid in Mexico; Mexican liability insurance is mandatory. After an accident you must report to police, and without insurance you may be detained and not allowed to leave until compensation is agreed. Carry an International Driving Permit.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Mexico

sentencing.name: Drug possession / trafficking (Mexico)
sentencing.mandatory_minimum: Pre-trial detention is common and can be lengthy.
sentencing.first_offender: Even small amounts can mean arrest, extortion risk, and long pre-trial detention for foreigners; a local lawyer is essential.

statutes.title: Carry your tourist permit (FMM/FMMD)
statutes.summary: Carry your FMM/FMMD and original ID as proof of legal status; officials may ask at checkpoints or on departure. Keep a copy of your passport separately.

statutes.title: Right to consular access when detained
statutes.summary: A detained foreign national may have their consulate notified and communicate with it — ask for this immediately if arrested.

book.title: Police, bribes, ID, and if you're detained in Mexico
book.overview: Mexico is a civil-law country. Carry your ID and FMM at all times. Some officers demand cash from tourists for minor things (public drinking, traffic) — you can decline and ask for a written fine or to go to the station. If detained, contact your embassy and a lawyer immediately. Emergency: 911.
your_rights: Carry your FMM/FMMD and original ID; officials may ask any time.
If an officer demands cash, you can refuse, note their name/badge/patrol number, say you will call 911, and request a written fine or to go to the nearest station.
Police may detain you up to 72 hours for petty offences.
If arrested, you have the right to a lawyer and to contact your embassy.
Do not sign anything without a lawyer and interpreter.
key_steps: Keep ID, FMM and a passport copy on you.
If asked for a bribe, stay calm, decline, and ask for a written fine or to go to the station.
If detained: ask for your embassy and a lawyer; say little.
Save 911 and the Embassy of Canada line (+52 55-5724-7900).
Note officers' details if anything feels wrong.
common_mistakes: Paying roadside bribes (encourages it and admits nothing good).
Handing over your passport to an officer.
Signing Spanish documents you don't understand.
Not contacting the embassy early when detained.
book.when_lawyer: If detained, arrested, in any drug matter, or after a serious accident: contact your embassy immediately and get a local lawyer. For a bribe demand, decline and escalate to the station rather than paying.

book.title: Entry, FMM, and your 180 days in Mexico
book.overview: You can usually stay up to 180 days, but the officer writes your actual allowed days — check it. Complete the FMMD online on arrival and keep it; you need it to leave. Extensions aren't possible from inside Mexico.
your_rights: Visa-free tourist stays up to 180 days (officer sets the number).
You're entitled to your entry record (stamp/FMMD) — verify the days granted.
You must keep your FMM/FMMD to exit.
key_steps: Complete the FMMD online on arrival; download and save it.
Check the days the officer actually granted.
Don't overstay — fines, detention, or deportation follow.
For longer stays, get Mexican immigration advice before your days run out.
book.when_lawyer: For overstays, status problems, or residency, consult a Mexican immigration lawyer; your embassy can provide a list.

sources.title: Government of Canada — Mexico travel advice

book.title: Arrested or charged in Mexico (esp. drugs)
book.overview: Mexico's system differs from common-law countries, pre-trial detention is common and can be long, and drug penalties are severe. Contact your embassy, get a local lawyer and interpreter, and say nothing without them.
your_rights: Right to a lawyer and to contact your embassy.
Presumption of innocence, but pre-trial detention is common — a lawyer helps seek release.
key_steps: Ask immediately to contact your embassy and a lawyer.
Do not sign or admit anything without counsel and translation.
Have someone notify family and the embassy's 24/7 line.
Avoid any involvement with drugs.
common_mistakes: Talking to police without a lawyer/interpreter.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately — a local criminal lawyer, with embassy help. Treat drug matters as an emergency.

sources.title: Government of Canada — Mexico travel advice

book.statute: Mexican Federal Penal Code; National Code of Criminal Procedure

book.title: Driving in Mexico — insurance and accidents
book.overview: Your Canadian insurance is not valid in Mexico. Mexican liability insurance is mandatory — buy it (at the border or online). After any accident, report to police; without insurance you may be detained and barred from leaving until compensation is agreed.
your_rights: You may drive on a valid foreign licence (carry an International Driving Permit too).
After an accident you must report to police and stay at the scene.
Your vehicle may be held and you may be detained until responsibility and fines are settled.
key_steps: Buy Mexican liability insurance before driving (full coverage with legal assistance is best).
Carry your licence, IDP, and insurance proof.
After an accident: call police, don't admit fault, contact your insurer's legal line.
Never drive after drinking — it voids insurance and is serious.
book.when_lawyer: After a serious accident or any detention, use your insurer's legal assistance and your embassy; get a local lawyer.

sources.title: Government of Canada — Mexico travel advice

book.statute: State traffic laws (Mexico); mandatory insurance rules

book.title: Emergencies and staying safe in Mexico
book.overview: For any emergency dial 911. Use registered taxis/rideshare, avoid displaying valuables, and keep your embassy's number handy. Some regions carry higher risk — check the current advisory before travelling within Mexico.
your_rights: Call 911 for police, fire, or ambulance.
Your embassy has a 24/7 line for citizens in distress.
You can report crimes and get a report for insurance.
key_steps: Save 911 and the embassy line.
After a crime, report it and get a written report.
Use hotel safes and registered transport.
In danger, call 911 first, then your embassy.
book.when_lawyer: For injury, a serious crime against you, or detention, contact your embassy for a referral to local lawyers.
